newsitem.title: USA: Republic sued by shareholder on AutoNation.
newsitem.headline: Republic sued by shareholder on AutoNation.

text.p: A Republic Industries Inc shareholder on Monday said he filed a lawsuit against the company, alleging securities law violations and breach of fiduciary duty regarding Republic's planned merger with AutoNation.
The plaintiff, David Jackowitz, said in a statement that the suit was filed on January 17 in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Florida and seeks class-action status.
A Republic spokesman declined to comment on the suit.

Among the named defendants are H. Wayne Huizenga, Republic's chairman and chief executive officer; and Steven Berrard, co-chief executive officer, president and a director of Republic, the statement said.
On January 16, Republic shareholders approved the acquisition of AutoNation, a used car retailing business controlled by Huizenga.

The lawsuit alleges that the stock transaction resulted in a "windfall" for AutoNation shareholders, which include Huizenga and Berrard, because of the sharp increase in the market value of Republic stock.
The lawsuit seeks, among other things, to recover damages on behalf of class members and to have the vote of the Republic shareholders approving the transaction to be null and void.
The plaintiff is represented by the law firm of Burt & Pucillo.
